---

Abstract

CourseWise is a conversational assistant for course information. A student asks a question in ordinary language; the assistant answers from a versioned corpus of course documents and shows the passage behind every claim, the document's publication date, and an explicit judgement of whether that document is still in force. The system is built around three commitments. First, an answer is never generated beyond the retrieved evidence: sufficiency is measured as IDF-weighted coverage of the question's own terms, and when coverage is insufficient the assistant refuses and explains which part of the question it could not support. Second, guidance that has been revised is handled explicitly. The corpus contains documents in several versions; conflict detection compares values by unit between versions, so a changed deadline, weighting, word limit or exam duration is reported to the student with both the old and the new value and the date of the replacement, while the superseded passage remains visible as flagged evidence. Third, the assistant cannot change anything on its own: requests that alter state follow a two-phase protocol in which the system previews the exact fields that would change, names the consequence, and writes nothing until the student confirms with a single-use token. The interaction is delivered through a web interface with an evidence panel that marks each passage as quoted, current or superseded. The current scope implements retrieval, policy assessment, extractive answer generation and the confirmation protocol. An LLM backend and email confirmation are specified but not built.

---

Design rationale and project explanation

The problem

Course information is scattered across documents that change without warning. A student who misses the revision of a brief learns the wrong deadline, plans for the wrong exam, and discovers the error after submitting. A conventional chatbot does not help: it answers fluently from a document that may no longer apply, and gives no indication of its own age. The problem is therefore not retrieval but currency — making it visible which guidance still applies.

The approach

The system separates four concerns. Retrieval finds candidate passages. A policy layer decides whether those passages may be used. Generation produces the answer from what survived. The interface shows the reasoning. Keeping freshness, conflict and sufficiency assessment outside the generation layer means the same guarantees hold whichever backend is selected.### Design choices

What was developed

The running system comprises a FastAPI backend over a corpus of twelve versioned documents, BM25 retrieval with synonym expansion and qualified-name phrase matching, a policy layer assessing freshness, conflicts and coverage, extractive answer generation, and the two-phase action protocol. The frontend renders the answer, an evidence panel marking each passage as quoted, current or superseded, and a confirmation card for state changes. Thirty-six automated tests cover retrieval ranking, freshness, conflict detection, refusal, the confirmation protocol and the HTTP contract.

How the work developed

The first retrieval implementation ranked a superseded Assignment 1 brief above its replacement, because the older text contained more occurrences of words like "supersedes". Version weighting was introduced in response. A second fault surfaced when a test showed a question about an "extension" failing to match a passage headed "Extensions"; a light stemmer was added. Conflict detection initially compared bare numbers and produced a false conflict about compulsory questions, which led to the unit-aware comparison. The warning layer grouped evidence by document key, collapsing a current version and its predecessor into one entry and hiding the warning about the old copy; grouping by version id corrected it. Each was found by a failing test rather than by inspection, which is the argument for the test suite being part of the deliverable.

Scope and limits

The corpus is a demonstration set authored for this module, not the live module page. Retrieval is lexical, so a question sharing no vocabulary with the documents will not find them, and refusal is the correct behaviour rather than a fallback. There is no user account system: bookings are a single shared list. The LLM backend and email confirmation are marked planned and are not part of the submitted build. ---

Design choiceWhy it suits the problemSupporting evidence or referenceStatus
Rank the version in force above the superseded version, rather than ranking on keyword overlap aloneBoth versions contain the same words, so raw overlap cannot distinguish them; an old copy can outrank the current one and propagate a withdrawn deadlineParasuraman & Riley (1997) distinguish misuse and disuse of automation — a system that acts on stale input is misusing it. Assignment 1 literature on automation biasImplemented
Compare conflicting values by unit, not by numberThe old and new exam briefs both state how many questions are compulsory; comparing bare numbers reports a change that never happened, which erodes trust in every other warningKocijan et al. (2023) argue explanations improve trust only when calibrated to the user's actual question; a false conflict is a failed explanationImplemented
Report a changed value as both values plus the replacement dateThe student needs to judge which value applies to them; the bare new value does not tell them their prior belief was wrong, and the bare old value misleadsJian et al. (2000) on trust and reliance: reliance must be calibrated against evidence, so the change has to be made legible rather than silently appliedImplemented
Refuse when the retrieved passages do not cover the question, and say which part is uncoveredA plausible answer with no source is worse than no answer, because a student cannot tell a guess from a citation; the failure mode of an assistant is confidently wrongSiau & Wang (2018) on transparency in algorithmic decision-making; Amershi et al. (2019) guideline 16 on making uncertainty legibleImplemented
Keep every factual claim traceable to a passage id, and mark the passages actually quotedTraceability is the only mechanism that lets a student verify an answer independently, and it converts the interface from an oracle into an instrumentLuger & Sellen (2016) on conversation design: grounding a response in retrievable material is what lets a user repair the exchangeImplemented
Require explicit confirmation, with a single-use token, before any state changesThe assistant reads policy the student may not have read; an action taken on a stale premise is hard to undo, and the cancellation deadline makes it worseParasuraman & Riley (1997): automation that acts rather than advises invites abuse; leaving the decision with the human is the augmentation caseImplemented
Keep the corpus small, versioned and inspectable rather than scraping the module pageA corpus the student can read lets the system be evaluated against known ground truth, which is what makes refusal and conflict detection testable at allAmershi et al. (2019) guideline 2 on making the system's capabilities legible at the point of useImplemented
Give every refusal a next step rather than a bare "I don't know"A refusal that dead-ends transfers the problem back to the student; one that names the documents or the team to contact preserves the interactionLuger & Sellen (2016) on repair: a usable turn offers a route forwardImplemented
Offer an LLM backend but keep it optional, with the extractive engine as defaultThe extractive engine is deterministic and inspectable, so behaviour can be asserted in tests; the LLM path improves fluency without weakening the constraints, which live in the policy layerKocijan et al. (2023) on rationale articulation: explanations are valuable when they are checkable, not because they are polishedSimulated
Send a confirmation email for a booked consultationThe handbook states bookings are confirmed by email and that a booking without a confirmation has not been placed, so email is part of the record, not a nicetyAssignment 1 development experience — the handbook's own wording forces thisPlanned
Allow students to compare two candidate readings side by sideWeek 3 reading lists alternatives for several topics; a single answer hides that the literature genuinely disagreesKocijan et al. (2023)Planned
